Position: Credit Analyst (CA)
Location: Lalitpur

About Us:

At Alaya, we pride ourselves on our guiding values of Care, Passion, and Oneness. We take pride in offering tailored solutions to our clients, helping them achieve their financial goals with confidence. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with like-minded individuals, celebrate your unique talents, and build meaningful professional connections.

Our dedication to employee well-being and success has earned us numerous awards, including the 2023 HRD Asia 5-Star Employers of Choice Award, the 2021 Liberty Australian Brokerage of the Year Award and the Best Community Engagement Program 2024.

About The Role:

As a Credit Analyst, you will play a critical role in supporting mortgage brokers through the assessment and submission lifecycle for the Australian home loan market. This role requires strong attention to detail, a sound understanding of lender policies, and the ability to complete accurate, compliant, and timely loan assessments.

You will be responsible for reviewing client files, assessing scenarios, preparing preliminary assessments and application forms, checking lender requirements, and identifying missing documents before submission. You will also work closely with brokers, Loan Processing Specialists, lenders, and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth file progression from assessment through to post-submission and post-settlement support.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex scenarios, working with detailed information, learning lender policies, and contributing to the quality and accuracy of mortgage brokerage services.

About You:

  • You thrive in a fast-paced environment where accuracy, compliance, and strong attention to detail are valued.
  • You take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks, and understand that even small documentation or data errors can lead to serious compliance risks.
  • You are proactive in finding solutions, asking the right questions, and contacting lenders or internal stakeholders to clarify requirements when needed.
  • You have a strong desire to learn and develop professionally, especially in credit assessment, lender policies, loan structures, and the Australian home loan market.
  • You communicate clearly and professionally with brokers, Loan Processing Specialists, and team members to ensure smooth coordination and timely file progression.
  • You are organised, dependable, and able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and accuracy in your work.
  • You collaborate well with others, support team success, and are open to sharing knowledge when required.
  • If you prefer routine tasks with limited learning or are not comfortable taking ownership of accuracy and compliance, this role may not be the right fit.

Major Deliverables:

  • Assess client files once completed forms and required documents are received.
  • Contact lenders to determine client eligibility and identify suitable loan structures.
  • Prepare preliminary assessments and application forms before submission.
  • Review lender checklists, identify missing documents, and complete required loan checklists.
  • Identify and address compliance issues and inform brokers accordingly.
  • Support brokers in maintaining existing client portfolios and ensuring timely post-settlement service.
  • Follow approved processes for documentation, data security, client confidentiality, and ISO 27001:2022 requirements.
  • Support team development through knowledge sharing and guidance to new team members when required.
  • Complete ad hoc tasks, projects, and related duties as assigned.

Requirements

Apply if you have:

  • Master’s degree running or completed in Finance, Business, Management, or a related field, ACCA candidates with no more than 3 papers remaining, or semi-qualified CA candidates.
  • At least 2 years of experience in the finance sector.
  • Top-notch written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, especially when reviewing loan files, documents, lender checklists, and compliance requirements.
  • Problem-solving ability and a solution-focused mindset.
  • General numerical and financial calculation skills.
  • Strong planning and organisational skills.
  • Ability to prioritise tasks and handle multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with accuracy and consistency.
  • A strong desire to learn and develop professionally, as there will be a significant learning curve.
  • Proficiency in Google Apps, including Google Drive, Docs, and Sheets.
  • Strong work ethics, accountability, and dependability.

Career Progression

The Credit Analyst role provides a strong pathway for professional growth within credit assessment, mortgage broking, and leadership functions.

With strong performance, continued learning, and demonstrated ownership, team members may progress towards roles such as:

  • Senior Credit Analyst
  • Mortgage Broker
  • Credit Team Leader or Manager

Benefits

Why should you join us?

At Alaya, we love the work we do and the colleagues we work with. We offer great growth and career advancement opportunities for our employees. While we operate in a fast-paced environment, we also value a supportive culture where people can learn, grow, and contribute meaningfully.

In this role, you will gain exposure to the Australian mortgage industry, develop strong technical knowledge in credit assessment, and play an important part in supporting brokers and clients through accurate and compliant loan assessments.

And yes, we work only 5 days a week!

What we offer:

Besides the list of benefits that the Labour Law mandates, we also offer:

  • Salary + Social Security Fund (SSF)
  • 5-day work week, Monday to Friday
  • Exclusive paid leaves
  • Conducive and fun working environment
  • Festival, profit, and book reading bonus
  • Team building activities and social events
  • Accidental and medical insurance coverage
  • International working environment exposure
  • Continuous learning and development opportunities

Plus, take advantage of our Customer Referral program to earn rewards by recommending our services to friends and relatives in Australia.

Our office is open, so if you’re selected, we’d be happy to work with you in person!

You also acknowledge and consent that your application may be reviewed and processed with the support of AI tools, and that certain stages of the recruitment process may include recorded transcriptions that may be processed through AI to support fair, accurate, and efficient recruitment decisions. Your data will be stored securely and will only be accessible to authorised personnel.

Ready to Apply?

If you’re looking for a role where your attention to detail, problem-solving ability, and willingness to learn can make a real impact, we’d love to hear from you.

Join us and be part of a team that values growth, collaboration, accuracy, and excellence.

Guided by the remarkable legacy of its co-founder, Helen Keller, Helen Keller Intl partners with communities striving to overcome longstanding cycles of poverty. By delivering the essential building blocks of good health, sound nutrition, and clear vision, we help millions of people create lasting change in their own lives. Working in 20 countries – across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the United States – and together with a global community of supporters, we ensure every person has the opportunity – as Helen did – to reach their true potential.

Brief Background: Helen Keller’s Nepal country office relies on a stable, secure information systems environment to support programs delivered across a range of locations, including districts with significant infrastructure challenges. This role ensures that staff have the technology support, network connectivity, and security practices they need to do their work effectively, while working closely with regional and global Information Systems colleagues to uphold organizational standards.

Purpose or Scope of work

The Officer, Information Technology oversees the country office’s information systems, working with regional and global colleagues to ensure network administration, hardware and application management, security, and user support are properly managed. The role requires a broad set of technical, planning, problem-solving, and hands-on support skills, along with the ability to work effectively in low-resource settings that present real infrastructure challenges. Above all, this position supports Helen Keller’s mission by keeping the technology that underpins our programs secure, reliable, and accessible, working collaboratively across a multicultural environment.

Management/ Functional Relationships

This role reports to the Senior Manager, Operations, with a dotted-line relationship to the Senior Manager, Information Technology. It works closely with regional and global Information Systems colleagues and collaborates internally with all Nepal-based staff. Externally, the role coordinates with partner organizations on network connectivity, as needed.

Application Deadline: August 30, 2026

Key Responsibilities/ Specific Tasks

  • Technical/Programmatic: Maintain and support information system components across Helen Keller’s Nepal offices, including hardware, applications, and network infrastructure, in line with global information systems standards.
  • Technical/Programmatic: Apply security patches and support security awareness initiatives to protect information systems and prevent security incidents.
  • Operations/Coordination: Manage information technology service requests through Helen Keller’s Fresh Service platform and coordinate escalations with regional technical support teams.
  • Operations/Coordination: Coordinate procurement and management of information technology assets across the country office.
  • External Engagement: Coordinate network connectivity support with partner organizations, as needed.

Other Duties

This job announcement is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities for the position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor.

Skills & Experience

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of technical management, information analysis, and computer hardware and software systems.
  • Hands-on experience with network installation, management, and data center governance.

Operational & Functional Skills

  • Excellent written and spoken Nepali and English language skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, and the ability to work independently in a dynamic, low-resource environment.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field required; or associate/technical diploma with 4+ years of directly related experience.
  • 3–4 years of relevant professional experience in an Information Technology support role, with a background in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related discipline.

Working Conditions/ Travel

  • Travel expectations: Occasional travel to district offices within Nepal to support network connectivity and hardware needs.
  • Work environment: Office-based role in a low-resource setting that requires adaptability and hands-on problem-solving.
  • Safeguarding responsibilities: Adherence to Helen Keller’s Code of Conduct and safeguarding policies.
  • Language requirements: Fluency in Nepali and English, written and spoken.

Expectations

Fairness, Belonging and Zero Tolerance to Abuse

As a member of the Helen Keller Family, each employee is expected to:

  • Help to develop and maintain an environment that welcomes and develops a multi-cultural workforce with varied lived experiences and identities.
  • Foster a work environment where everyone feels valued and included.
  • Support employees’ evaluation and promotion processes based on skills and performance.
  • Promote a safe, secure, and respectful environment for all members of Helen Keller family, stakeholders in general, and particularly for the communities we serve.
  • Follow Helen Keller Code of Conduct helping to prevent any type of abuse including workplace harassment, sexual abuse and exploitation, and trafficking in persons.
  • Adhere to the Organizational Core Values, which include courage, compassion, integrity and rigor.

To Apply

Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter and resume to Nepal.Recruitment@hki.org. Applications will be accepted until August 30, 2026. Click here to view the detailed Job Description.

Organization Description

The Why: NEPAL aspires to graduate from least developing country to a lower middle-income country by 2026. However, the development community’s excessive focus today on socio-political empowerment has not yielded the desired economic transformation. In reaching the 2026 national target, shall we wait for institutions of power to become accountability productive or shall we bolster innovations of people to bring inclusive prosperity? How do we strengthen grassroots-government collaboration in shaping an equal and enterprising future?

The How: DAAYITWA, with a focus on economic empowerment, envisions an enterprising Nepal where every youth has opportunities for a prosperous future. Daayitwa is a part of the Daayitwa Abhiyaan which consists of four organizations: Daayitwa, Governance Lab, Nepal Leadership Academy based in Nepal and Nepal Rising (Daayitwa-US) based in the U.S. Inspired by shared values of innovation, collaboration, and service, it promotes the socio- economic development of Nepal. The movement fosters inclusive and equitable economic growth by accelerating grassroots innovations, strengthening government institutions, and revitalizing a virtuous cycle of democracy and development through grassroots-government collaboration.

Our Focus Areas:

1. Promote enterprise-led employment creation

2. Design evidence-based policies for improved decision-making

3. Build state capability for effective policy implementation

4. Foster stakeholder collaboration for governance innovations

Daayitwa runs several programs and initiatives aimed at our focus area.

Job Description

The What: We are looking for a full-time Research Associate who will (a) work closely with a research team based at top international universities to develop study protocols (b) collaborate with on-ground policy partners to execute the study and collect monitoring data; and (c) collect, clean and analyse data from large-scale field surveys in our study sample. The Research Associate will be based in Kathmandu, with occasional travel to study field sites. This position requires a self-starting candidate, who enjoys working on cutting edge research that informs policy. The candidate will have a unique opportunity to drive efforts to ensure that government policy priorities inform research agenda and vice versa. The candidate will also conduct in-depth interviews and scoping activities, engage with government stakeholders, manage field activities and coordinate field staff for the execution of primary data collection activities. She/he will support high-quality cleaning and rigorous analysis of both primary and secondary data, and work with a team of leading economists and public policy experts from top universities across the world and the Inclusion Economics India Centre. It is an excellent opportunity for someone interested in a career in academic research to work closely with a Principal Investigator team that includes Rohini Pande (Yale University) Maulik Jagnani (Tufts University), and George Taylor (UC Berkeley).

The Project:

Urban and peri-urban flooding imposes severe and growing economic costs across South Asia, with the burden falling disproportionately on the informal firms that form the backbone of local economies. Kathmandu’s peri-urban and urban economy is built on a dense population of informal firms whose financial fragility makes flood disruption acutely damaging and adaptation especially difficult; evidence from similar settings shows that firms systematically underinvest in protection even when adaptation would be cost-effective, and the evidence base on why — and what would shift their behaviour — remains thin. This proposal outlines a randomised study testing whether timely flood forecast information allows formal and informal firms in Kathmandu to take anticipatory measures to prevent flood damages, generating evidence to support climate-resilient economic growth in Nepal.

The central question is whether information constraints are the binding obstacle to adaptation among Kathmandu’s peri-urban formal and informal firms. Treatment firms receive timely forecast dissemination, and the study measures outcomes including days of business closure, inventory losses, worker layoffs, and changes in procurement and sales patterns, as well as relevant outcomes for neighbouring firms, connected suppliers, workers, and consumers.

Responsibilities:

In collaboration with the research and senior project teams, the Research Associate will be required to:

  • Conduct data cleaning and analysis of multiple primary and secondary data sources.
  •  Seek out and collect administrative data from partners and government agencies.
  • Assist in the design and field-testing of scoping and survey instruments.
  • Support the day-to-day implementation of field-based research including scoping, surveying,field staff recruitment, training & supervision.
  • Support with writing research outputs such as policy briefs, research articles, etc.
  •  Review and report on academic literature of requested topics in support of concept notes, policy briefs and research projects.
  • Manage day-to-day relationships with officials at all three spheres of government, policy and program partners in academia, civil society etc., as requested.
  • Others, as required

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree with experience in data-based research, preferably in economics, political economy, political science, or a related field.
  •  Strong interest in public policy and economic development in low-income countries.
  •  Excellent oral and written communication skills in Nepali and English languages.
  •  Proficiency in Stata and/or other statistical tools and the Microsoft Office suite.
  • Mature, self-directed individual with ability to balance multiple tasks and prioritize effectively to meet deadlines in a fast-paced working environment.
  • Ability and willingness to travel regularly and frequently to other parts of the country.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with data based research in Stata and/or other statistical tools is highly desired.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to engage with partners at various levels.
  • Additional local language skills (apart from English and Nepali).
  •  Field experience and administering surveys will be an added advantage.
  • Prior experience with external stakeholder engagement such as government, donors, development agencies, and/or political parties.

What we offer

  • A dynamic and engaging environment within our office in Kathmandu, with our India based partner, and with internationally acclaimed researchers.
  •  A competitive salary by local standards.
  •  Regular travel within Nepal.

Additional information

Compensation: Governance Lab will provide compensation on a monthly rate basis. The rate will be mutually agreed upon, commensurate with the level of the required deliverables, the qualifications and experience of the candidate.

Posiiton: Disaster Risk Management Specialist-Heat Lead
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to working areas

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action – helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future. Mercy Corps has been operating in Nepal since 2005, implementing programs in food security, agriculture, market development, financial services, youth engagement, climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. We take a systems-based approach in our programming, with the aim of improving the lives and potential of vulnerable individuals and communities across Nepal.

Program/Department Summary

The Zurich Climate Resilience Alliance (ZCRA) is an alliance of nine organizations including international NGOs, private sector, and academic organizations, who have come together with the support of the Zurich Foundation to drive better policy and practice to reduce the negative impact of floods on peoples’ and communities’ ability to thrive.

The Alliance is implementing a 12-year vision through 2025. The current phase (phase 3, 2024-2027) represents the first cycle of this long-term vision. Previously, the Alliance completed its first phase in 2018, and its second phase in December 2023 and third phase will run till Dec 2027. During this time, The Alliance works together to achieve 12-year vision by implementing solutions, promoting good practice, influencing policy and facilitating systemic change. In Nepal, the Alliance is comprised of Mercy Corps and Practical Action, working together on joint outcomes aiming at:

  • Building ex-ante resilience of communities at risk of flood and heat impacts across Nepal
  • Improving early warning and early action in advance of probable hazards
  • Enabling people who experience livelihoods losses due to floods and heat to recover quickly through compensation and/or insurance

General Position Summary

The Disaster Risk Management Specialist – Heat Lead will serve as Mercy Corps’ technical lead on heat resilience, providing technical expertise and coordination to strengthen the management of extreme heat risks across programmes and partnerships in Nepal. The position will lead the design, implementation, and quality assurance of heat resilience interventions and support the integration of heat risk management into disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, health, urban planning, livelihoods, and resilience programming. Working closely with government agencies, technical institutions, development partners, academia, the private sector, and communities, the Heat Lead will strengthen heat governance, policy, planning, early warning systems, and sustainable financing while promoting gender equality, disability inclusion, and locally led approaches. The role will also lead research, knowledge management, capacity strengthening, technical advocacy, and resource mobilization to enhance evidence-based programming and support the scale-up of heat resilience initiatives in Nepal. While heat resilience will be the primary technical focus of the position, the Specialist will also provide technical support to broader disaster risk management programming, including flood and wildfire resilience initiatives, ensuring integrated multi-hazard approaches across Mercy Corps’ resilience portfolio.

As gender and social inclusion (GESI), governance and environmental compliance are cross-cutting and core components of all MC programs and is required to own these components to ensure GESI sensitivity and integration, governance practices and environmental compliance are integrated into the program activities.

Essential Job Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Disaster Risk Management Specialist -Heat Lead include, but are not limited to, the following:

1. Technical Leadership, Thought Leadership and Program Development (25%)

  • Serve as Mercy Corps’ technical focal point on heat resilience and provide strategic leadership across program components.
  • Provide thought leadership on heat resilience by promoting innovative approaches, generating evidence, influencing national discourse, and positioning Mercy Corps as a leading technical partner on heat risk management in Nepal.
  • Lead the design, implementation, and quality assurance of heat resilience interventions, ensuring alignment with national priorities and global good practices.
  • Provide technical guidance on integrating heat risk management and GESI considerations into DRR, climate adaptation, health, urban planning, livelihoods, and resilience programming to ensure inclusive and equitable outcomes.
  • Develop technical tools, training packages, guidance notes, methodologies, and standards on heat to support program implementation.
  • Identify emerging trends, best practices and opportunities for innovation and scaling of heat resilience interventions through research, technology, partnerships, and adaptive programming.
  • Lead and contribute to technical publications, policy briefs, conference presentations, webinars, and knowledge-sharing events to advance learning and influence policy and practice on heat resilience.
  • While leading Mercy Corps’ heat resilience portfolio, provide technical support to flood, wildfire, and other multi-hazard disaster risk management initiatives, promoting integrated and risk-informed approaches across programs.

2. Heat Governance, Policy and Systems Strengthening (25%)

  • Support federal, provincial and local governments to strengthen institutional mechanisms for heat governance.
  • Lead technical support for the development and implementation of Heat Action Plans (HAPs), heat governance strategies, technical guidelines, and standard operating procedures.
  • Strengthen integration of heat risk management into disaster management, climate adaptation, health, urban development, and sectoral plans.
  • Support the development and strengthening of heat early warning systems, impact-based forecasting, and preparedness protocols in collaboration with technical agencies.
  • Support the integration of heat priorities into government planning, budgeting, budget advocacy, expenditure tracking, and climate finance mechanisms to strengthen sustainable investment in heat resilience.
  • Support community empowerment on heat resilience through awareness campaigns, risk communication, behaviour change initiatives, and community engagement, ensuring vulnerable groups have the knowledge and capacity to prepare for, respond to, and adapt to extreme heat.
  • Promote the integration of GESI considerations into heat governance, policies, plans, and institutional mechanisms to ensure that the needs and priorities of women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups are addressed.
  • Provide technical support for heat-responsive planning, budget advocacy, and expenditure tracking at federal, provincial, and local levels to strengthen investment and accountability for heat resilience.
  • Coordinate and strengthen partnerships with government institutions, including Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration, National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, the Ministry of Health, provincial governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector.
  • Support the establishment and strengthening of multi-stakeholder coordination platforms and communities of practice to promote collaboration, knowledge exchange, and coordinated action on heat resilience.
  • While leading heat resilience initiatives, provide technical support to the integration of flood, wildfire, and other priority hazards into government policies, plans, and coordination mechanisms to strengthen multi-hazard disaster risk management.

3. Program Implementation, Capacity Strengthening and Partnership (25%)

  • Lead heat hotspot mapping, vulnerability assessments, heat studies and research to inform program design and policy.
  • Provide technical oversight for the implementation of Heat Action Plans and community-based heat resilience interventions, ensuring they are gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, and accessible to vulnerable populations.
  • Support implementation of heat mitigation measures including cooling centres, nature-based solutions, drinking water facilities, heat-resilient infrastructure, and public awareness initiatives etc. and ensure effective implementation in accordance with program standards and global best practices.
  • Support implementation of heat resilience interventions that strengthen the resilience of local enterprises, workers, and markets to extreme heat.
  • Build the capacity of government officials, municipalities, health workers, schools, community disaster management committees, media, and partner organizations on inclusive heat risk management, ensuring meaningful participation and leadership of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Foster partnerships with research institutions, academia, private sector actors, and technical organizations to promote innovation and collaboration.
  • Lead the planning, coordination, and facilitation of heat resilience workshops, consultations, and technical dialogues at federal, provincial, and local levels.
  • Provide technical support to the design, implementation, and quality assurance of flood, wildfire, and other multi-hazard resilience interventions, as required, ensuring alignment with program standards and integrated disaster risk management approaches.

4. Knowledge Management, Monitoring and Resource Mobilization (20%)

  • Lead research, documentation of program learning, evidence, case studies, technical reports, and knowledge products.
  • Monitor implementation progress, analyse program performance, and support adaptive management.
  • Develop and track program indicators related to heat resilience and contribute to monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) processes.
  • Prepare technical inputs for donor reports, presentations, policy briefs, and communication products.
  • Represent Mercy Corps in national and international technical working groups, forums, and coordination platforms related to heat and climate resilience.
  • Contribute to proposal development, technical design, and resource mobilization efforts to expand Mercy Corps’ heat resilience portfolio.
  • Promote cross-learning and knowledge sharing across heat, flood, wildfire, and other disaster risk management programs to strengthen integrated multi-hazard resilience programming.

Others

Conduct himself/herself both professionally and personally in such a manner as to bring credit to Mercy Corps and to not jeopardize its humanitarian mission.
Mercy Corps as a humanitarian agency is expected to response as and when crisis and humanitarian situation engulfs. As an MC employee, all staff are expected to be part of humanitarian and emergency response in addition to their regular roles and responsibilities in such situations.
Other duties as assigned by the Country Director.

Security

Proactively ensure that team members operate in a secure environment and are aware of policies.

Accountability to Beneficiaries

  • Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our beneficiaries and to international standards guiding international relief and development work, while actively engaging beneficiary communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.
  • Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values always and in all in-country venues.

Supervisory Responsibility: N/A

  • Reports Directly to: CRC Program Manager
  • Works Closely with: Province Coordinator(s), Senior Advocacy and Influencing Officer, Private Sector Engagement Specialist, Implementing Partners, Mercy Corps’ cross functional departments, other programs, ZCRA Alliance III partners – Practical Action etc.

Knowledge and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change, Environmental Science, Urban Planning, Engineering, Geography, or a related field.
  • At least 6 years of experience in disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate change adaptation, resilience, or related fields, including at least 3 years of specific experience in heat resilience or extreme heat programming.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing Heat Action Plans, heat resilience strategies, or related policies and programs.
  • Strong knowledge and experience of heat risk assessment, vulnerability analysis, early warning systems, impact-based forecasting, and climate data interpretation.
  • Proven experience in conducting research, synthesizing technical evidence, and translating research findings into practical recommendations, policies, and programs design.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing high-quality knowledge products, including technical reports, policy briefs, guidance notes, case studies, training materials, and communication products.
  • Experience in knowledge management, documentation of lessons learned, evidence generation, and facilitating learning and knowledge-sharing processes.
  • Strong experience working with federal, provincial, and local government institutions, technical agencies, and development partners.
  • Strong facilitation, stakeholder engagement, partnership development, and capacity-building skills.
  • Excellent analytical, coordination, project management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent report writing, technical writing, and verbal communication skills in both English and Nepali.
  • Experience integrating GESI principles into disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, or resilience programming.
  • Experience working with international NGOs, bilateral or multilateral donors, or donor-funded program.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Success Factors

A successful candidate will have the ability to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment with a capacity to spark innovative approaches to programming and inspire groups to collaborate closely to implement high-quality programs. They will have a proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions

The position is based in Kathmandu, and it requires up to 50% travel to support country programs.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

Achieving our mission begins with how we build our team and work together. Through our commitment to enriching our organization with people of different origins, beliefs, backgrounds, and ways of thinking, we are better able to leverage the collective power of our teams and solve the world’s most complex challenges. We strive for a culture of trust and respect, where everyone contributes their perspectives and authentic selves, reaches their potential as individuals and teams, and collaborates to do the best work of their lives.

We recognize that diversity and inclusion is a journey, and we are committed to learning, listening and evolving to become more diverse, equitable and inclusive than we are today.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

We are committed to providing an environment of respect and psychological safety where equal employment opportunities are available to all. We do not engage in or tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, disability (including HIV/AIDS status), marital status, military veteran status or any other protected group in the locations where we work.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members must complete mandatory Code of Conduct eLearning courses upon hire and annually.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

Resilience Coordinator, RAIN Project

S/He will be involved in overall management of adaptation components, technical leadership, capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and collaboration with implementing partners to ensure evidence-based and scalable adaptation strategies. S/He will provide technical guidance to DCA, team and partners, as well as ensure that activities are implemented timely and to a high standard while ensuring linkages with deliverables under Early Warning System – Early Adaptation, inclusion, localization and Shock Responsive Social Protection. The position is based at Janakpur, RAIN Consortium Office but has to travel both Madhesh and Lumbini Provinces.

  • Provide technical leadership on all adaptation and specific resilience activities
  • Supervise the design and implementation of locally-led adaptation interventions
  • Co-develop and deliver training with support from partner’s Adaptation Coordinator to CBOs and local governments on climate adaptation and its strategies.
  • Build capacity of CBOs and LG’s of RAIN in risk-informed planning, climate-smart practices, and leveraging fiscal resources for adaptation.
  • Lead the implementation of adaptation and specific resilience activities including supervising and closely collaborating with partner staff for this component; guiding and supervising Adaptation Coordinators as well as collaborating with LG Officers based at the local government level.
  • Together with DCA Climate Action Advisor and implementing partners, provide capacity building to DCA staff, consortium partners, CBOs and relevant stakeholders on adaptation and components of resilience and develop high-quality training materials and curricula.
  • Contribute to the Resilience Measurement Framework together with RAIN MEAL Lead and EWS EA Lead.
  • Collaborate closely with the Climate Action Advisor, Consortium Manager and DCA’s Global Advisers in developing knowledge products, and internal, governmental and donor reports, together with reporting to other stakeholders/groups (technical working group, clusters).
  • Represent DCA and RAIN project professionally with external stakeholders, including government, non-governmental agencies and donors especially in Madhesh and Lumbini, and especially to stakeholders in adaptation and resilience
  • Together with MEAL lead and Communication & Advocacy Manager, engage in project-learning-based positioning and advocacy, development of learning papers and selection of advocacy points for SARATHI, as per Country Strategy

Qualification, Skill and Knowledge:

  • Master’s degree in civil engineering, climate change, natural resource management, disaster risk management, environment science or relevant field, with 5 years of work experience with an I/NGO or development organization in the area of climate adaptation and resilience.
  • Strong track record in designing and leading climate adaptation and resilience initiatives in Nepal, engagement with regional and global adaptation and resilience programmes is an advantage.
  • Expert knowledge and experience in watershed management and application of nature-based solutions in river basin management and its linkages with ecosystem services
  • Experience working with diverse stakeholders in climate change, DRRM and AA sector, especially with local, district, provincial and federal level actors.
  • Commitment to systems strengthening approaches, proven track record in adaptive management and facilitation approach for adaptation and resilience in Nepal.
  • Experience in field-based understanding of vulnerabilities, exposure and risk in the multi-hazard context of Nepal.
  • Experience in watershed management and application of nature-based solutions in river basin management and its linkages with ecosystem services
  • Construction experience (bioengineering designs, safe shelter construction, and other mitigation efforts) is an advantage.
  • Sound knowledge of existing climate resilience frameworks.
  • Demonstrated experience in coordinating diverse teams and maintaining strong relationships with the project team, partners and local stakeholders.
  • Outstanding communications and networking skills; with a strong command of Nepali and English languages- written and spoken.

Posiiton: ECA & CCA Coordinator
Location: Lalitpur

The ECA & CCA Coordinator is responsible for planning, coordinating, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating all Extra Curricular Activities and Co-Curricular Activities of United Academy and United College. The position is responsible for ensuring that ECA and CCA programs are well planned, student focused, safe, financially responsible, and aligned with the institution’s academic and student development objectives.

Key Result Areas and Responsibilities

1. Annual Planning and Activity Coordination

  • Develop and maintain the annual ECA and CCA calendar in consultation with the Academic Head and Principal.
  • Plan a balanced range of academic, sports, cultural, artistic, recreational, leadership, and skill based activities.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments, teachers, instructors, student representatives, and external organizations for the successful implementation of activities.
  • Ensure that all planned activities are conducted smoothly and within the approved schedule.
  • Review the ECA and CCA calendar periodically and recommend necessary changes based on institutional requirements and student interests.
  • Develop activity plans, timelines, manpower requirements, logistical arrangements, and other requirements for each major activity.

2. Student Engagement and Participation

  • Promote active student participation in ECA and CCA activities.
  • Identify students’ talents, interests, skills, and areas of potential through participation in various activities.
  • Encourage wider participation by identifying barriers to student participation and developing appropriate initiatives to address them.
  • Coordinate and provide guidance to student clubs, committees, teams, and activity groups.
  • Maintain participation records for each activity and monitor participation trends.
  • Develop strategies to increase student participation in ECA and CCA programs.
  • Encourage students to participate in internal and inter level competitions, exhibitions, performances, tournaments, and other events.

3. Budget and Resource Management

  • Prepare the annual and activity specific budget requirements for ECA and CCA programs.
  • Obtain prior approval for budgets and expenditures before implementing activities.
  • Coordinate with Procurement, Store, Finance, and other relevant departments for the timely availability of required resources.
  • Ensure effective and economical utilization of the approved budget and resources.
  • Maintain proper records of expenditure and supporting documents for each activity.
  • Identify opportunities to maximize the impact of activities while maintaining cost effectiveness.

4. Manpower and Logistics Coordination

  • Assess and plan the manpower requirement for each ECA and CCA activity.
  • Coordinate with teachers, instructors, support staff, volunteers, security personnel, transport teams, and other relevant personnel as required.
  • Ensure appropriate allocation of responsibilities before and during each activity.
  • Coordinate venue arrangements, equipment, materials, transportation, accommodation, refreshments, and other logistical requirements where applicable.
  • Ensure that all activities are adequately staffed and operationally prepared.

5. External Resource Person and Guest Coordination

  • Establish and maintain professional relationships with sports persons, artists, trainers, coaches, industry professionals, guest lecturers, and other relevant external resource persons.
  • Coordinate with external resource persons regarding their availability, participation, requirements, and schedules.
  • Maintain an updated record of visiting resource persons, guest lecturers, trainers, coaches, and other external contributors.
  • Prepare reports and maintain supporting documentation for activities involving external resource persons.
  • Explore opportunities to introduce new experts and professionals who can add value to student development programs.

6. Safety, Compliance and Risk Management

  • Ensure that appropriate safety measures are implemented for all ECA and CCA activities.
  • Conduct basic risk assessment and identify potential safety concerns before activities are conducted.
  • Coordinate with relevant personnel to address identified safety risks.
  • Ensure that activities comply with the policies, procedures, rules, and standards of United Academy College.
  • Ensure appropriate supervision of students during activities, events, tours, field trips, competitions, and other programs.
  • Immediately report any significant safety, disciplinary, or operational concern to the Academic Head or Principal.

7. Event and Competition Management

  • Plan and coordinate ECA and CCA events, competitions, exhibitions, showcases, tournaments, performances, and other student activities.
  • Ensure smooth coordination of schedules, venues, participants, judges, coaches, guests, equipment, and other requirements.
  • Coordinate internal and interlevel competitions and encourage increased student participation.
  • Maintain records of participation, results, achievements, awards, and recognitions.
  • Facilitate appropriate recognition and celebration of students’ achievements.
  • Conduct post event reviews to identify strengths, challenges, and areas for improvement.

8. Educational Tours and Field Trips

  • Coordinate the planning and execution of educational tours, field visits, excursions, and other off campus student activities.
  • Maintain proper records of educational tours and field trips, including participants, destination, dates, responsible personnel, and relevant reports.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments and service providers for logistical arrangements.
  • Ensure appropriate student supervision, safety, documentation, and compliance with institutional requirements.

9. Communication and Promotion

  • Communicate ECA and CCA schedules, requirements, notices, and updates to students, teachers, staff, and parents where applicable.
  • Promote ECA and CCA programs to encourage student participation.
  • Coordinate with the Brand, Engagement, Communication, and relevant teams for appropriate promotion and documentation of activities.
  • Ensure timely communication of activity related information to all concerned stakeholders.
  • Support the development of appropriate promotional and informational materials for major ECA and CCA activities.

10. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting

  • Monitor the implementation and effectiveness of ECA and CCA activities.
  • Collect feedback from students, teachers, parents, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Analyse participation levels, student satisfaction, achievements, and outcomes of activities.
  • Identify activities with low participation and recommend strategies to improve engagement.
  • Prepare a report for each major ECA and CCA activity.
  • Prepare periodic consolidated reports covering activities conducted, participation, achievements, expenditure, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Review the effectiveness of ECA and CCA programs and recommend improvements for future activities.

11. Documentation and Record Keeping

  • Maintain accurate and updated records of all ECA and CCA activities.
  • Maintain records of student participation, competitions, achievements, awards, guest lecturers, resource persons, educational tours, field trips, and major events.
  • Maintain activity plans, approved budgets, reports, attendance records, photographs, certificates, results, feedback, and other supporting documents.
  • Ensure that ECA and CCA records are systematically maintained and readily available when required.
  • Maintain a database of student participation and achievements for institutional reference.

12. Continuous Improvement

  • Develop new ideas and initiatives to make ECA and CCA activities more effective and engaging.
  • Identify emerging interests and opportunities in sports, arts, culture, technology, leadership, communication, and other areas relevant to student development.
  • Benchmark suitable activities and practices from other educational institutions where appropriate.
  • Recommend new activities based on student feedback, participation trends, institutional priorities, and available resources.
  • Continuously review existing activities and recommend discontinuation, modification, or expansion based on their effectiveness.

Expected Deliverables

The position holder shall be responsible for ensuring the following key deliverables:

  • Annual ECA and CCA Calendar
  • Activity wise plans and schedules
  • Activity wise budget proposals and approvals
  • Manpower and logistics plans
  • Student participation records
  • Guest lecturer and external resource person records
  • Educational tour and field trip records
  • Activity reports and supporting documentation
  • Student feedback and satisfaction analysis
  • Participation and achievement analysis
  • Periodic ECA and CCA performance reports
  • Recommendations for improvement and development of ECA and CCA programs

JOB SPECIFICATION

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Management, Education, Sports Management, Event Management, or a relevant discipline. A Master’s degree will be an advantage.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 2 to 3 years of relevant experience in ECA/CCA coordination, student activities, event management, sports, education, or a similar role, preferably within an educational institution.

Technical Competencies

  • Good knowledge of ECA and CCA planning and implementation.
  • Good event planning and coordination skills.
  • Ability to prepare activity plans, budgets, schedules, and reports.
  • Good knowledge of student engagement and activity management.
  • Basic knowledge of safety and risk management for student activities.
  • Proficiency in MS Office and Google Workspace.
  • Ability to maintain systematic records and documentation.

Core Competencies

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Student engagement and relationship management.
  • Planning and organizational ability.
  • Coordination and teamwork.
  • Problem solving and decision making.
  • Time management and multitasking.
  • Creativity and initiative.
  • Accountability and result orientation.

Preferred Attributes

  • Passion for student development and extracurricular activities.
  • Interest or experience in sports, arts, culture, music, or other student activities.
  • Ability to work with students of diverse interests and abilities.
  • Ability to coordinate with teachers, parents, external resource persons, and service providers.
  • Willingness to work beyond regular hours during events, competitions, tours, and special programs when required.

Personal Attributes

  • The position holder should demonstrate professionalism, discipline, patience, adaptability, enthusiasm, integrity, and a positive attitude toward students and colleagues.

Position: Project Coordinator (Policy Advocacy)

NEEDS Nepal is a non-profit, non-governmental social organization that has been actively working in the social sector for the past 27 years. The organization was established in 1999 as a youth group and has since then engaged in various social transformation, good governance, and development initiatives. NEEDS Nepal is registered with the Government of Nepal. It has partnered with numerous governments, I/NOGs, and bilateral agencies to implement programs that focus on empowerment, socio-economic development, safe shelter and social transformation for marginalized and vulnerable communities such as children, women, youths, persons with disabilities, Dalits, Janajati and other marginalized groups. NEEDS Nepal has four working themes identified through the organizational strategy plan 2024-2028: Social Justice and Rights, Climate & Disaster Resilient Action, Dignified Migration & Livelihood, and Organizational Development.

Project Brief

NEEDS Nepal, in partnership with Habitat for Humanity Nepal, is implementing the Surakshit Awash Program (SASWIN, SAFER and SABAL projects) in Kanchanpur district, Sudurpashchim province Nepal. The project aims to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable communities by promoting safe housing, disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate resilience, and inclusive community development. The SASWIN project focuses on strengthening policy and legal frameworks, enhancing institutional capacity, promoting evidence-based advocacy, and facilitating collaboration among provincial and local governments to improve access to land and housing rights. The project is being implemented in Bedkot Municipality and Shuklaphanta Municipality of Kanchanpur District. In this context, NEEDS Nepal has announced a vacancy notice for the position of Project Coordinator (Policy Advocacy). The detailed job description can be accessed through the link.

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KJGMPB2KY3Bfy9Ww8p_slJQyrwfry0ol?usp=drive_link

Safeguarding & PSEA

NEEDS Nepal has a zero-tolerance policy and approach to any abuse, sexual harassment, or exploitation of a vulnerable adult or child by any of our staff, volunteers, consultants, and suppliers. All individuals and institutions have committed to respecting the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the organization’s safeguarding policy, Zero Tolerance Policy, PSEA & code of conduct that is associated with the organization.

NEEDS Nepal expects all the staff to share this commitment through Safeguarding, PSEA Policy, and Code of Conduct. All staff must be committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants, or others, are treated with respect and dignity.

How to apply

Qualified & eligible national citizens are highly encouraged to apply with their updated CV along with a motivation letter & expected salary in gross per month to the following email address, hr@needsnepal.org.np by 17th August 2026.

Women, ethnic minorities, and local applicants are highly encouraged to apply. No telephone calls will be entertained, and this automatically disqualifies in the recruitment process.

NEEDS Nepal will reserve all rights to make the final decision. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the further recruitment process. The remuneration and other benefits package shall be as per NEEDS Nepal HRM policy & guidelines.

ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP’s values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.
  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.
  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.
  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.
  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).
  • WFP encourages female candidates and people with disabilities to apply.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

Job holders at this level demonstrate responsibility and initiative to respond independently to queries with only general guidance. There is a requirement to use judgment in dealing with unforeseen problems on a daily basis. Job holders have a level of expertise and knowledge to adapt and contribute to the development of systems and processes to continually improve the level of support provided. Job holders manage resources, and coach and coordinate with relevant security staff and with a team of travel support staff. These jobs may require reporting for duty on short notice. The incumbent reports to the Management Services Officer.

JOB PURPOSE:

To provide support and perform administration related duties and responsibilities. The incumbent will be the focal person for travel of WFP Country Office Nepal and coordinate security-related support services with the United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) which include performing tasks related to the implementation of security measures. The position is equivalent to job category of Management Services Associate.

TERMS AND CONDITION

Position Title: Administrative Associate (Admin/Travel)

Contract Type: Special Service Agreement (SSA L6)
Level: SSA L6

Contract Duration: 6 months

Duty Station: Kathmandu, Nepal
Deadline of Application: 17.08.2026

WFP offers a competitive benefits package including salary plus CIGNA health insurance.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (not all-inclusive, nor exhaustive):

1). Coordinate administrative and technical support within the Management Services portfolio to ensure efficient and high-quality service delivery.

2). Monitoring resources needs with designated areas of responsibilities (travel, security, facilities, assets, etc.) and assist in identifying new requirements to enhance operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness of services. Review and recommend improvements to relevant SOPs and procedures.

3). Collate and analyze relevant data and prepare and/or consolidate reports to contribute to decision-making and efficient management of resources.

4). Monitor and process actions related to procurement, finance and other relevant areas. Liaise with other functions and third-party contractors to enable efficient service delivery and seek better prices for travel as per WFP liability.

5). Process Trip documents for international air ticket issuance ensuring correct DSAs.

6). Utilize digital tools and technology applications to improve working practices and customer service and effectively adopt new technologies that are introduced at the workplace.

7). Participate in the preparation of inter-agency initiatives as part of UN Reform to achieve cost savings and enhancement of service quality.

8). Provide support to emergency preparedness and response by allocating resources, offering analytics, on related services.

9). Act as security focal person. Collate and analyze information from UNDSS and prepare and or consolidate reports to contribute to decision making and efficient management of resources.

10). Liaise with UNDSS in order to co-ordinate with local administration, security and law enforcement authorities, communities, UN/NGO security staff and other actors for safer programme delivery as required.

11). Support in reviewing security related information (e.g. security incidents and events, security support for daily activities, etc.). Update the security focal point at the Headquarters/Regional Security Advisor on security developments on a day-to-day basis.

12). Plan and co-ordinate staff activities during field missions and support in performing security assessments within the area of responsibility to support safe and effective programme delivery.

13). Assist the MS (Administration) Officer on security risk management matters and safety issues in compliance with the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) and support the implementation of risk management mitigation measures, including Minimum Operational Security Standards (MOSS) to ensure compliance.

14). Support the maintenance and management of security equipment and make recommendations to strengthen technology capacity in line with business requirements.

15). Monitor and ensure that all access control procedures are effective and stringently followed by all staff and visitors, to maintain a safe and secure environment.

16). Attend security meetings and coordinate with security focal points of other UN Agencies as and when required.

17). Train and guide the travel-related Business Support Assistants within other functional units in the area of work ensuring travel objectives are met in line with required standards.

18). Provide orientation to all staff to improve understanding of WFP travel regulations, policies, procedures, processes, standards, and systems. Review security training needs to develop measures to meet business requirements, liaise and coordinate with UNDSS for security training to staff.

19). Act as alternate in absence of Fleet Focal Point and perform duties as required.

Experience:

  • Sound understanding of general travel regulations, policies, procedures, processes, standards and systems.
  • General knowledge of procedures and systems used in security, asset and facility management.

Desired Knowledge & Skills:

  • Sound knowledge of travel related functions gained through relevant technical training or experience.
  • Ability to monitor and record travel related financial transactions.
  • Has experience in collating data and preparing reports pertaining to admin portfolio.
  • Has experience in coordinating the work of others and providing guidance and training.
  • Has experience working with teams across different functional areas.
  • Ability to manage emergency situations and remain calm.
  • Excellent communication skills to maintain frequent correspondence with both, internal staff and external authorities.
  • General knowledge and understanding of security administration, risk assessment and co-ordination with local authorities and local law enforcement agencies.
  • Attention to detail and constant vigilance in order to promptly detect any breach in security measures.

Languages:

Job Description

Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Chief Migration Health Officer (CMHO) and direct supervision of the Senior Laboratory Technologist, the incumbent will be responsible for technical support to laboratory services with respect to Migration Health Assessments (HAP) and other programmes implemented by the IOM Migration Health Division in country Kathmandu, NEPAL.

Responsibilities

1. Perform laboratory procedures as assigned by the laboratory supervisor for pre-examination, examination, and post-examination activities through the use of the standard relevant equipment.

2. Contribute to the implementation of laboratory quality management systems under the guidance of the laboratory supervisor. Take on the focal point role for one or more quality system essentials (QSE) as requested by the laboratory supervisor.

3. Ensure standards and the quality of laboratory procedures by strictly following the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

4. Adhere to biosafety measures adopted in the laboratory, being responsible for the safety of oneself and others.

5. Organize and operate activities on assigned station for accurate, efficient and timely delivery of results.

6. Perform quality control and quality assurance activities for assigned stations and document results as required.

7. Facilitate laboratory equipment maintenance to ensure these are in good working order and operate equipment appropriately following SOPs.

8. Facilitate laboratory stock management and monitor that the equipment and consumables are sufficient for the anticipated work.

9. Alert the laboratory supervisor to any problems related to operations, including equipment, stock management and biosafety.

10. Facilitate maintenance of established systems of organized record keeping and information management for timely delivery of results, data collection, analysis and reporting for laboratory monitoring and facilitation of operational research.

11. Develop and/or update SOPs in coordination with the laboratory supervisor.

12. Participate in the improvement of the service system according to the adopted work plan in the laboratory.

13. Manage and meet client expectations by prioritizing interests and providing services with guiding principles of patients’ dignity, beneficence and non-maleficence in courteous manner.

14. Ensures compliance with IOM instruction INS 278 and undertakes all designated mandatory trainings.

15. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or Diploma from an accredited academic institution in Medical (Clinical) Laboratory Sciences, Microbiology or a related discipline in countries where the scope of responsibilities are fulfilled according to national regulations.
  • A valid license to practice is required.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Three years for Bachelor’s degree holder and five years for diploma holders of relevant clinical laboratory experience in a busy institution, preferably in a laboratory;
  • Relevant technical knowledge and practices to personnel and laboratory operations;
  • Knowledge and experience in clinical laboratory techniques;
  • Knowledge of laboratory quality management systems;
  • Knowledge of the principles and practices laboratory biosafety;
  • Computer literate with understanding of accurate data collection and analysis for monitoring and continuous improvement of laboratory services and performances; and,
  • Good awareness of the laboratory role in health systems, optional use of resources for quality and efficient services delivery;
  • Proven laboratory expertise and/or advanced degree in laboratory specialization is an advantage.

Skills

  • Effectively applies and transfers relevant technical knowledge and practices to personnel and laboratory operations
  • Organizational skills;
  • Communication skills.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM’s official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and Nepali language is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

The Organization:

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2011. Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health and its fundraising brand Corus World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. In Nepal, Corus operates under Lutheran World Relief. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.

At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. We promote an engaging and supportive work environment, where employees feel enabled and driven to innovate, learn and collaborate. And because our subsidiaries often function as partners, our employees have the opportunity to work across our enterprise family.

Job Brief:

Position Summary: This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.

The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people.
