FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations.

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind.

Organizational setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

The main aim of the FAO Country Offices, which are headed by FAO Representatives (FAORs), is to assist governments to develop policies, programmes and projects to achieve food security and to reduce hunger and malnutrition, to help develop the agricultural, fisheries and forestry sectors, and to use their environmental and natural resources in a sustainable manner.

Specific activities of the Country Offices include:

  •  Implementing FAO’s field projects and participating in the development of the Field Programme by identifying” and formulating new projects and liaising with local donor representatives.
  • Helping governments to prevent and assess the damage of disasters and assisting them in the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the agricultural sector.
  •  Carrying out public awareness activities and support important FAO campaigns such as the World Food Day (WFD).
  •  Providing assistance to technical and investment missions from FAO headquarters and from Regional or Subregional Offices to the country.
  •  Serving as a channel for FAO’s services to governments and other partners (donors, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), civil society organizations (CSOs), research institutions, etc.).
  • Keeping FAO informed of major social and economic developments in the country and monitoring the situation of the agriculture sector in the country.
  • Acting as FAO Representative to host governments and all partners involved in FAO activities.

Reporting Lines

The Young Professional Officer (Climate Change and Natural Resources Management) reports to the Assistant FAO Representative (Programme) and collaborates closely with the relevant Climate Change Project leads in close collaboration with other programme colleagues.

Technical Focus

The Young Professional Officer (Climate Change and Natural Resources Management) assists with the development and implementation of FAO programmes and activities related to climate change and natural resources management in Nepal. More specifically, he/she will assist the project leads to manage climate change adaptation, mitigation and resilience interventions within FAO Nepal’s agriculture, forestry and sustainable natural resource management sectors, aligning with government priorities and in line with the priorities set forth by FAO Nepal’s Country Programming Framework (CPF) (2023-2027).

Key Results

Research, technical analysis and project related services to support the delivery of assigned projects, products and services.

Key Functions

  • Analyses relevant technical social, economic, environmental, and technology information, data and/or statistics for input in various documents.
  •  Maintains records and updates databases and web pages.
  •  Provides technical support to various projects.
  •  Collaborates in the development of training tools and materials and the organization of workshops/seminars, etc.
  • Participates in the organization and follow-up of meetings, consultations and conferences, the production of required materials and the provision of information and assistance to partners.

Specific Functions

  • Assists in the coordination and implementation of ongoing (National, Regional and Global) climate change-related programmes and projects in the areas of agriculture, forestry, and natural resource management.
  •  Supports the preparation of concept notes and project proposals in the areas of climate change and natural resource management, as well as related resource mobilization efforts.
  •  Supports the programme leads in monitoring projects, including compiling inputs for revisions, tracking expenditures and resources, and flagging potential discrepancies against budget lines.
  • Assists in maintaining the completeness and quality of data and documentation in FAO’s corporate systems for assigned operational field projects and activities.
  • Participates and assists in supporting the development of partnerships with relevant organizations and stakeholders, including government agencies, UN agencies, NGOs, and the private sector.
  • Participates and assists in the organization of policy dialogues, workshops, and consultation meetings in coordination with the programme team and stakeholders.
  • Contributes to stakeholder engagement and awareness-raising activities, including preparation of communication and outreach materials; and
    Performs other related duties as required.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

  •  Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in areas such as agriculture, climate change, environmental science, natural resource management or any other fields.
  •  One year of relevant experience in supporting including exposure to the implementation of climate change and natural resource management projects and programmes.
  •  Working knowledge of English (proficiency – Level C) and intermediate knowledge (intermediate proficiency – level B) of another FAO official language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish).

Competencies

  •  Results Focus
  • Teamwork

  • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  • Extent and relevance of experience in related fields such as climate change, natural resource management, food and nutrition security, agricultural development and disaster risk reduction
  •  Extent and relevance of experience in the preparation, editing and revision of technical/scientific documents and in organizing meetings and workshops
  •  Extent and relevance of experience in supporting partnerships with UN agencies, NGOs as well as donors and government institutions and agencies
  •  Working knowledge of another FAO language would be an asset
  •  Work experience in more than one location or area of work, particularly in field positions, is desirable.

The Copywriter is responsible for bringing eSewa brand to life through impactful storytelling and compelling copy that inspires action and builds emotional connections with customers. The role goes beyond writing as it requires translating marketing strategies into meaningful narratives that seamlessly connect visuals with words, ensuring every communication reflects eSewa’s brand promise.

Working closely with designers, marketers, product teams, and business stakeholders, the Copywriter will create audience-centric communication that resonates across customer segments, occasions, and platforms.

Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Mass Communication, Journalism, English, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 1–3 years of experience in copywriting, content writing, advertising, digital marketing, or brand communication.
  • Experience in fintech, banking, technology, consumer brands, or advertising agencies will be an added advantage.

Job Description

  • Develop compelling copy for integrated marketing campaigns, product launches, seasonal campaigns, and always-on brand communication.
  • Craft engaging content for social media, digital advertisements, app banners, landing pages, websites, blogs, emailers, SMS, push notifications (FCM), in-app communication, video scripts, press releases, and other marketing assets.
  • Partner closely with designers to ensure copy and visuals work together to tell a cohesive, emotionally engaging story rather than functioning as separate elements.

Background: The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive change. ADRA Nepal belongs to the worldwide ADRA network, comprised of more than 100 supporting and implementing country offices. Operating in Nepal since 1987, ADRA has been a trusted partner for 40+ years in health, livelihoods, education, and disaster risk management. It collaborates with all levels of government and civil society, focusing on Madhesh, Bagmati, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim Provinces, with presence in 150+ municipalities across 20 districts.

Required positions: The following four (4) positions are required for the delivery of Institutional Service for Quality Improvement in Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC) and Sick Newborn Care Units (SNCUs) in Lumbini Province. Periodic field visits for supervision and joint monitoring.

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promotes integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

The Junior Technical Assistant (Livestock/ veterinary) will provide field-level technical

Job Summary

support to livestock farmers and entrepreneurs under the SaBaS Project. The position will promote livestock farming practices and support enterprise development through regular technical guidance, training, monitoring, and coordination with local stakeholders. This
reflects the typical role of JTAs in Nepal’s livestock and livelihood projects.

Primary Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

  •  Conduct regular field visits to monitor the health and condition of livestock and poultry.
  •  Provide basic veterinary first aid and technical support within the scope of VJTA responsibilities.
  •  Identify common signs and symptoms of livestock and poultry diseases and provide appropriate technical advice.
  •  Support disease prevention, control, and management activities.
  •  Assist in vaccination, deworming, parasite control, and other animal health campaigns as authorized.
  •  Maintain proper records of animal health services provided.
  •  Identify complicated or emergency cases and refer them to a qualified veterinarian or appropriate veterinary service provider.
  •  Provide technical advice to farmers on scientific livestock management practices.
  •  Promote improved cattle, buffalo and goat management practices.
  •  Support farmers in improving animal housing, sanitation, hygiene and biosecurity.
  •  Provide technical guidance on breeding, reproduction and general livestock management.
  •  Coordinate with livestock section on palika level or ward level.
  •  Coordinate with supervisor for taken proper guidelines and support.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Qualifications and Experience

  •  Diploma/JTA/ TSLC in Livestock/ veterinary science from a recognized institution.
  •  2 years of relevant work experience in livestock, animal health, veterinary services, farmer mobilization, or community-based livestock programs.
  •  Good knowledge of livestock health, disease prevention, vaccination, deworming, animal nutrition, breeding, husbandry and basic veterinary practices.
  •  Field experience: Experience working directly with farmers, livestock groups and rural communities will be an advantage.

  •  Valid two-wheeler driving license with willingness to travel extensively within Kapilvastu is preferred.

Posiiton: Children’s Home Associate
Location: Surkhet, Karnali

“A world where every child is safe, educated, loved”- Kopila Valley Sewa Samaj is a non-profitable NGO registered in Surkhet, Nepal to provide support for children and families in our community. Our mission is to change the world by empowering Nepal’s children. KVSS programs include a residential children’s home, Kopila Valley School (KVS) for inclusive quality education, women’s empowerment, sustainability, health and wellness, and family development programs. We provide our students with free education, educational materials, health treatment and medicine, counseling, and a place to live. With our innovative future program, we strive to provide our children with career guidance, and scholarships for further studies. Our children’s home provides a safe, loving, and stable home for children in extreme cases of need, when all other options have been exhausted. We do this with our funding partner BlinkNow Foundation and in close ties with the local government and communities.

Position Summary-

The Staff working at KVSS should have patient and passionate about working with children will thrive as childcare. Should be enthusiastic about the growth and well-being of Children, sensitive to their needs, able to mix, relax and interact socially with children and be linked and respected by Children. The Children Home Associate at Children’s Home is responsible for the care, wellbeing, and upbringing of the children living within the KV Children’s Home. Your role is to provide basic parental, pastoral, and holistic care to provide the children with the brightest future possible. It is also your responsibility to manage and coordinate with all the other staff members working within the KV Children’s Home, and make sure that all caregiving roles are running as smoothly as possible.

The Employee will be required to perform the following duties and undertake the following responsibilities in a professional manner.

Job Description

The Main Responsibilities

  • Make sure that the children at KV Children’s Home are cared for and supported in the best way possible.
  • Support to manage caregivers and other support team members.
  • Assist in enrichment activities of the children.

Detailed Responsibilities

1.Make sure that the children at Kopila Valley Children’s Home are cared for and supported in the best possible way.

  • Create and update routines for the activities of children in Kopila Valley Children Home, and make sure that they are followed properly.
  • Lead daily gathering (sutsang) for children after dinner.
  • Manage activities that are designed to promote physical, mental, and social development of children.
  • Support children in their education- ensure that they study for an appropriate period regularly, and manage interactive activities and support children to learn, grow and feel proud.
  • Support children to make sure that they are done with all the chores that they are supposed to do before school
  • Performing regular check-in with the children in a one-to-one format in order to provide support and engage their needs.

2.Support to manage caregivers and other support team members.

  • Supervise the work of caregivers at the children’s home daily and provide continued feedback for any improvements required to improve services.
  • Coordinate with the admin team in regards to any necessary items for children.
  • Demonstrate discipline from personal behavior, initiate it for the team to demonstrate, and encourage it to flow from the team to the children.
  • Support caregivers to address any obstacles or challenges they may face.
  • Evaluate the performance of the home caregivers and support them in their professional development.
  • Coordinate with relevant team members to run all other children’s home functions smoothly.

3.Assist in Academic and non academic activities of the Children

  • Support children during their home works and study time.
  • Assist in non academic activities as planned by the Enrichment coordinator.
  • Prepare engagement activities independently during their free time with the support of caregivers.
  • Ensure that children’s study time tables are duly followed as per the time table.

Additional expectations

  • Take ownership of change and engage and encourage innovation.
  • Build positive working relationships and environment in the organization by bringing solutions to the discussion table.
  • Report to the manager on a weekly basis, and as needed in case of urgent activities.
  • Build and maintain a strong relationship with the children, staff and relevant stakeholders.
  • Attend weekly staff meetings and share operational updates.
  • Always maintain integrity and confidentiality.
  • The above list of responsibilities is not comprehensive, and candidates may be required to take on additional responsibilities, as determined by your supervisor.

Must Have

  • Education: +2 in Social science or any discipline.
  • Experience: At least 3 years of proven experience in a residential care or child protection field
  • Language: A good communicator, fluent in Nepali and basic in English
  • Skills and Abilities: Ability to manage, mentor and lead children, youth, their activities
  • Passionate about and cares for children and vulnerable population; initiator, and competent in managing caregivers, children and basic operations.
  • Works collaboratively and independently with the least supervision required.

Note: This is a residential and immersive role where the Children Home Associate needs to be hands on caregiving as well. Preferred Female.

Key Characteristics

  • You believe that we can change the world, in the blink of an eye
  • You believe in making decisions that put children first
  • You are self-motivated, organized, and approachable
  • You enjoy creating systems, keeping records, and increasing efficiency
  • You are always looking for new ways for our team to work smarter instead of harder
  • You are detail-oriented and conscientious. You make sure nothing slips through the cracks
  • You have a strong work ethic and a willingness to pick up new skills. You are comfortable multi-tasking
  • You are positive, patient, and a clear communicator who is comfortable working with both Kopila Valley staff in Nepal and the BlinkNow staff in the United States
  • You are an empathetic person, with a knack for putting out fires before they start and soothing conflicts brewing beneath the surface
  • You require little supervision and are flexible. You understand that you will be wearing many hats in this role, many of which are not explicitly included in this job description

Application Procedure

If you think this career opportunity will amplify your career growth, we encourage you to apply by clicking “Apply for this Job” and submit all required document. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for further screening process. No telephone inquiries will be entertained. We accept and screen applications on a rolling basis.

Position: Junior Technical Assistant (Agriculture)
Department: Program
Project/Program: Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) Project
Reports to: Technical Coordinator (Enterprises Development)
Duty station: KIDS Central Office, Taulihawa, Kapilvastu, Lumbini Province
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable
and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promotes integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

The Junior Technical Assistant (Agriculture) will provide field-level technical support to

Job Summary

farmers, producer groups, and agri-entrepreneurs under the SaBaS Project. The position will promote climate-smart agriculture, improve productivity, strengthen market-oriented farming practices, farmer field school and support enterprise development through regular technical guidance, training, monitoring, and coordination with local stakeholders.

This reflects the typical role of JTAs in Nepal’s agriculture and livelihood projects.

Primary Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

  •  Involvement in assessing livelihood opportunities through agriculture and assessing their feasibility.
  • Provide technical advisory services to farmers and producer groups on climate-resilient agriculture practices.
  • Conduct agriculture related training, farmer field school, demonstrations plots, develop model farms, field visits, and technical coaching.
  •  Support the distribution of agricultural inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, and tools to beneficiaries.
  •  Support the establishment and strengthening of farmer groups, cooperatives, and agri-enterprises.
  •  Conduct regular field visits to monitor crop performance and provide timely recommendations.
  •  Assist in implementing project activities related to enterprise development, value chains, and market linkages.
  •  Collect field data, maintain records, and prepare monthly progress reports.
  •  Monitor crop performance, identify production constraints, and recommend appropriate technical solutions.
  •  Coordinate with local governments, agriculture offices, cooperatives, and other stakeholders.
  •  Support in linking farmers to markets, input suppliers, and financial institutions.
  •  Ensure gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and environmental sustainability are integrated into project activities.
  •  Perform other project-related duties assigned by the supervisor.
  •  Prepare periodic reports and share key findings with the Livelihood Coordinator.
  •  Represent the organization in community and palika level in agriculture related meetings and events.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Qualifications and Experience

  • Diploma/TSLC /JTA in Agriculture (Plant Science) from a recognized institution.
  • At least 2 years of experience in agriculture extension, community mobilization, or livelihood projects.
  •  Good knowledge of vegetable production, integrated pest management (IPM), climate-smart agriculture, and farmer training.
  •  Strong communication and facilitation skills in Nepali; knowledge of local languages is an advantage.
  •  Valid two-wheeler driving license with willingness to travel extensively within Kapilvastu is preferred.

Application Instructions:

Interested candidates are requested to apply via email with a recently updated CV and cover letter by 12th August 2026 to: procurement.kids@gmail.com

More information: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17ATa3uulyEtqbujjdzn6AQswmkZC2Vo5?usp=sharing

  • Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for further selection process
  • Telephone enquiry will not be entertained

Position: Procurement & Logistics Officer
Department: Administration Depart
Project/Program: Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) – Project
Reports to: Senior Administrative & Finance Officer / Executive Director
Duty station: KIDS Central Office, Taulihawa, Kapilvastu, Lumbini Province
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration
Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering an equitable, healthy, resilient, and self-reliant society. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized
communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implement development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health,
Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promote integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

Job Summary

The Procurement & Logistics Officer is responsible for supporting the efficient planning, implementation, and monitoring of procurement, logistics, inventory, asset management, and fleet operations for organizational and project activities. The position
ensures that all procurement and logistics processes are conducted in compliance with the policies and procedures of Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS), donor requirements, and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.

The Procurement & Logistics Officer coordinates the procurement of goods, works, and services through transparent, competitive, and value-for-money processes. The position is responsible for maintaining procurement documentation, managing supplier relationships, coordinating logistics arrangements, monitoring inventory and fixed assets, and ensuringthe timely delivery of supplies to support effective project implementation.

Working under the direct supervision of the Administration & Finance Manager/Senior Administration & Finance Officer (or designated supervisor), the Procurement & Logistics Officer collaborates closely with programme, finance,
administration, and field teams to ensure that procurement and logistics services are responsive to operational needs and donor compliance requirements. The position is expected to maintain high standards of integrity, accountability, confidentiality, and professionalism while contributing to efficient resource management, operational excellence, and the achievement of organizational objectives.

Primary Responsibilities

A. Procurement Management

  • Implement procurement activities in accordance with the organization’s Procurement Policy, donor regulations, and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.
  • Prepare and update procurement plans in coordination with project and support teams.
  • Receive, review, and process approved procurement requests ensuring completeness and budget availability.
  • Obtain quotations, conduct market surveys, and prepare comparative bid analysis to ensure competitive and value-for-money procurement.
  • Prepare Requests for Quotation (RFQs), purchase orders, purchase agreements, and other procurement documentation.
  • Coordinate bid opening, quotation evaluation, supplier selection, and procurement committee meetings as required.
  • Ensure procurement processes are transparent, fair, and properly documented.
  • Follow up with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of goods and services according to agreed specifications and delivery schedules.
  • Maintain procurement records and filing systems in both hard-copy and electronic formats.
  • Assist in preparing procurement reports and procurement status updates.

Logistics Management

  •  Coordinate the transportation, delivery, receipt, and distribution of project materials, equipment, and
    supplies.
  • Arrange logistics for meetings, workshops, training programs, field visits, and project events.
  • Ensure timely delivery of procurement items to project sites and end users.
  • Coordinate transportation arrangements for staff, consultants, visitors, and project activities as required.
  • Monitor delivery schedules and resolve logistics issues to minimize delays.

C. Inventory and Asset Management

  •  Maintain updated inventory records for office supplies, equipment, and project assets.
  •  Receive, inspect, record, and issue materials in accordance with organizational procedures.
  •  Conduct periodic physical stock counts and reconcile inventory records.
  •  Maintain an updated fixed asset register and ensure all assets are properly tagged.
  •  Report damaged, obsolete, or missing assets to the supervisor and support disposal processes in accordance with organizational policies.
  •  Ensure safe storage and proper handling of inventory and organizational assets.

D. Fleet and Office Support

  •  Maintain vehicle logbooks and monitor vehicle utilization, fuel consumption, servicing, insurance, and registration.
  •  Coordinate routine maintenance and repairs of vehicles and office equipment.
  •  Monitor office supplies and initiate procurement requests to maintain adequate stock levels.
  •  Support office administration by coordinating courier services, mail, office maintenance, and utility services when required.

E. Vendor and Contract Management

  •  Maintain an updated database of approved suppliers, contractors, and service providers.
  •  Assist in evaluating supplier performance and maintaining supplier records.
  • Monitor supplier deliveries and contract performance to ensure compliance with agreed terms and conditions.
  •  Coordinate with vendors to resolve delivery, quality, or service-related issues.

F. Compliance, Documentation, and Reporting

  •  Ensure procurement and logistics activities comply with organizational policies, donor requirements, and Government of Nepal regulations.
  •  Maintain complete procurement, logistics, inventory, and asset documentation for audit and donor review.
  •  Support internal audits, external audits, and donor monitoring visits by providing required documentation.
  •  Prepare monthly procurement, logistics, and inventory reports for management.
  •  Ensure proper filing and record retention in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

G. Coordination and Communication

  •  Coordinate closely with Finance, Administration, and Program teams to ensure timely procurement and logistical support for project implementation.
  •  Liaise with suppliers, transport providers, government offices, and service providers regarding procurement and logistics matters.
  •  Participate in procurement committee meetings and provide administrative support as assigned.
  •  Communicate procurement progress and delivery status to relevant staff on a regular basis.

H. Safeguarding, Ethics, and Organizational Compliance

  • Comply with the organization’s Code of Conduct, Procurement Policy, Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Corruption Policy, and other
    organizational policies.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, fairness, confidentiality, and value for money in all procurement and logistics activities.
  • Ensure all work is carried out with integrity and in accordance with donor requirements and organizational standards.
  •  Maintain confidentiality of procurement information and supplier documentation.
  •  Contribute to a safe, respectful, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.
  •  Perform any other procurement, logistics, or administrative duties assigned by the Supervisor, Project Coordinator, or Executive Director that are consistent with the nature of the position.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Education

  •  Bachelor’s degree in business administration/ management from a recognized university.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in procurement, logistics, administration, or supply chain management, preferably in NGOs, INGOs, or donor-funded projects.
  •  Experience in implementing procurement processes, logistics coordination, inventory management, and vendor management.
  •  Experience in preparing procurement documentation, maintaining procurement records, and supporting procurement committee processes.
  •  Experience in coordinating transportation, delivery of goods, and warehouse or inventory management.
  •  Familiarity with donor-funded project procurement procedures is desirable.

Knowledge

  •  Good knowledge of procurement principles, logistics operations, inventory control, and asset management.
  •  Understanding of procurement policies, competitive bidding procedures, and value-for-money principles.
  •  Familiarity with the procurement requirements of donor-funded projects and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.
  •  Basic knowledge of contract management, supplier relationship management, and procurement documentation.
  •  Understanding of workplace health and safety, safeguarding, and ethical procurement practices.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  •  Ability to maintain procurement tracking sheets, inventory records, and asset registers.
  •  Experience using inventory management systems, procurement software, or ERP systems will be an advantage.
  •  Good record-keeping, filing, and documentation skills.
  •  Ability to prepare procurement reports and maintain accurate procurement and logistics records.

Core Competencies

  •  Procurement and Logistics Coordination
  •  Inventory and Asset Management
  •  Planning and Organizational Skills
  •  Attention to Detail
  •  Time Management and Ability to Meet Deadlines
  •  Problem Solving and Decision Making
  •  Communication and Interpersonal Skills
  •  Teamwork and Collaboration
  •  Integrity, Accountability, and Professional Ethics
  •  Adaptability and Willingness to Learn

Language Requirements

  •  Good written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  •  Ability to prepare procurement correspondence, reports, and official documentation in English.

Personal Attributes

  •  Honest, reliable, and committed to maintaining confidentiality.
  •  Strong organizational skills with attention to accuracy and detail.
  •  Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
  •  Ability to manage multiple tasks and work under pressure to meet deadlines.
  •  Commitment to transparency, accountability, safeguarding, and the values and mission of Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS).

Application Instructions:

Interested candidates are requested to apply via email with a recently updated CV and cover letter by 12th August 2026 to: procurement.kids@gmail.com

  • Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for further selection process
  • Telephone enquiry will not be entertained

Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child

KIDS promote integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

Job Summary

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) Officer has a role in planning organizing carrying out and making better the Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) system for the Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) and
Sponsorship Communication Project. This role makes sure that program data is collected, checked, studied understood and sharedin timely manner with the relevant stakeholdesr. The position helps in making timely informed decisions which allows the program to act according to program information/dataway,The position also work according to the donor requirements- and learn more as an organization.

The MERL Officer is in charge of creating and using monitoring plans, tracking numbers, making sure that the collected data is efficient, effective and correct. With the use of digital tools the position is responsible in checking the data quality through regular checks, data triangulation and source data verification. The role maintains the data base in order which supports in writing relevant reports and internal and external sharing documents with special emphasis on knowledge sharing so that the program can be more effective and impactful.

This position works under the guidance of the Project Coordinator. Works closely with the teams that handle the program, safety, sponsorships and technical issues. The MERL Officer makes sure that everything follows the rules of KIDS, the MERL standards of
Plan International Nepal what the donors want and the rules from the Government of Nepal. The role also helps with being responsible by making community feedback systems making sure data is honest keeping private data safe and helping the people working on the project and the partners learn more about the tools, ways and standards for MERL. By checking all the time making sure the information is correct and learning from the work the MERL Officer helps reach the goals of the project make the program better.
Help children, young people, families and communities, in the project areas.

Primary Responsibilities

A. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

  •  Develop periodic MERL work plans that match project objectives and donor requirements.
  • Maintain and regularly update project monitoring tools, indicator tracking systems and reporting mechanisms.
  • Regular monitoring of project outputs, outcomes and impact indicators and informing the program on timely basis.
  • Against the set targets check the performance of the project and suggest changes to make the program better and more effective.

The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.
KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.
KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. ActionAid is a global justice federation committed to advancing social justice, gender equality, and the eradication of poverty. Established in 1972, the organization has continuously evolved to address the systemic drivers of inequality and injustice. ActionAid’s core belief is that people living in poverty and exclusion hold the power to create meaningful change within their families, communities, and societies. Since the 1990s, ActionAid has embraced a Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) to development, and in 2003, the ActionAid International federation was formed, now headquartered in South Africa.

ActionAid International Nepal (AAIN), a member of this global federation, was established in 1982 as a social justice organization working across multiple provinces of Nepal. AAIN actively engages in national and international social justice movements and collaborates with networks, alliances, and civil society coalitions. Through an HRBA framework, AAIN empowers marginalized communities to claim their rights and challenge the root causes of poverty, exclusion, and injustice. As part of the global federation, AAIN works with partners worldwide to promote social justice, gender equality, poverty eradication, and climate justice.

The Project Finance Officer is responsible for supporting effective financial and grant management of externally funded programmes that contribute to climate resilience, Ecosystem-based Adaptation, and sustainable development, in alignment with ActionAid International Nepal’s (AAIN) Strategy 2029.

The position ensures sound financial management, planning and budgeting, grant management, financial and donor reporting, with AAIN policies and procedures, donor requirements, and applicable laws and regulations while providing technical and operational support to implementing partners to strengthen financial management, internal controls, and compliance, and contributes to strengthening AAIN’s financial systems, internal controls, and institutional financial sustainability as a member of the Finance Sustainability Unit.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support finance team, programme team and partner organization on the planning and budgeting for both AAIN and Partners level following the organizational standards, donor’s requirements and applicable financial guidelines
  • Conduct and contribute to the review and consolidation of AAIN’s annual plans and budgets while providing technical support to Partner Organisations in the development of work-plan and budget from externally funded programmes
  • Support the line manager in analyzing and mitigating foreign exchange gain/loss implications during budget preparation and budget revisions.
  • Provide updated funding information, in consultation with the Line Manager to Head of Finance Sustainability and Administration (HoFSA) to support informed planning and budgeting decisions.
  • Monitor the financial performance of externally funded projects and provide regular financial status updates and analysis to the Line Manager, Finance Sustainability Unit and programme team.
  • Conduct periodic financial monitoring and compliance reviews of implementing Partner Organizations through monitoring visits, desk reviews and other appropriate mechanisms to ensure compliance with donor requirements, organisational policies and procedures, and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Track and follow up on the implementation of agreed corrective actions at both Partner Organisation and AAIN levels to ensure timely resolution of audit, monitoring, and compliance findings.
  • Support on Due diligence Process of partners as required
  • Timely and accurate recording of all income and expenditure transactions in the accounting system.
  • Perform periodic bank and account reconciliations and provide alternative for resolution of discrepancies.
  • Monitor and report exchange gains/losses related to project funds.
  • Support the timely updating of financial information in the CMS system.
  • Maintain adequate cash flow to facilitate the smooth implementation of programs and projects.
  • Provide accurate and timely financial information and reports to the Line Manager, finance team, program team and other stakeholders as required.
  • Support on SWC or regulatory body compliances like as periodic reports/CPAC/MPAC/evaluations etc.
  • Allocate and distribute common/shared costs across projects periodically in accordance with organizational policies, guidelines, and standard practices.

Requirements

  • Has knowledge about different donors’ requirements and compliance
  • Has good knowledge about effective communication among teams, partners and relevant groups
  • Has knowledge of operating accounting software it’s workflow to maintain financial records and transactions

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in finance/management/Commerce or equivalent from a recognized university
  • Master’s degree in finance, Accounting or Financial Management, Qualification such as ACCA, CA, CPA qualification are preferable
  • At least 3-5 years of relevant experience

Location: Kathmandu, Nepal

Deadline: Thursday 13th August 2026

ActionAid is a global justice federation committed to advancing social justice, gender equality, and the eradication of poverty. Established in 1972, the organization has continuously evolved to address the systemic drivers of inequality and injustice. ActionAid’s core belief is that people living in poverty and exclusion hold the power to create meaningful change within their families, communities, and societies. Since the 1990s, ActionAid has embraced a Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) to development, and in 2003, the ActionAid International federation was formed, now headquartered in South Africa.

ActionAid International Nepal (AAIN), a member of this global federation, was established in 1982 as a social justice organization working across multiple provinces of Nepal. AAIN actively engages in national and international social justice movements and collaborates with networks, alliances, and civil society coalitions. Through an HRBA framework, AAIN empowers marginalized communities to claim their rights and challenge the root causes of poverty, exclusion, and injustice. As part of the global federation, AAIN works with partners worldwide to promote social justice, gender equality, poverty eradication, and climate justice.

Climate Resilience & Research Manager:

Conceptualize, plan and manage research and programme initiations to promote resilience against disaster, and Ecosystem-based Adaptation and ensure humanitarian response in case of any emergency to contribute to overall organisational mission to achieve social justice, gender equality and poverty eradication in line with ActionAid International Nepal (AAIN)’s Strategy 2029.

This position leads and directs the work of AAIN in accordance with sound management practices and ActionAid’s development policies and accountability systems
  • Develop, monitor, review and update the research activities, Climate, DRR and Humanitarian related activities, work plan to ensure that the theme attains its objectives as cost-effectively and efficiently as possible
  • Coordinate with Organizational Impact and Innovation (OII) department in monitoring and evaluating programmes and projects related to Climate, DRR and Humanitarian
  • Document and disseminate thematic learning from the programme and share with programme team and OII department.

Position Title: MEAL Officer (Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning) Officer
Project: SAMBHAV JEEVAN: Enabling Better Lives through Sight and Sound
Reports to: Project Manager, SAMBHAV JEEVAN
Duty Station: NNJS Project Office, Birendranagar, Surkhet with regular travel to all project catchment areas in Karnali Province
Supervises: No direct reports; works closely with project team, the Disability Inclusion Officer and the Admin & Finance Officer for data inputs
Contract Type / Duration: Full-time, fixed-term project position aligned with the project cycle; subject to performance and continued project funding

Background

Karnali Province continues to face a high burden of preventable and treatable eye and ear health problems, particularly among populations living in remote and hard-to-reach areas. Limited availability of specialized services, weak referral systems, and geographic barriers have resulted in inadequate access to quality care for the majority of communities. In this context, there is a critical need to design, plan, and implement comprehensive community-based eye and ear care interventions. The proposed project aims to strengthen early detection, expand outreach services, and improve access to affordable and inclusive care, ensuring that underserved populations in Karnali can receive timely and effective eye and ear health services.

Position Purpose

The MEAL Officer is responsible for designing, operating and continuously improving the project’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning system; for the timely and accurate collection, management and analysis of disaggregated project data; for producing the project’s MEAL-related reports on schedule; and for ensuring that communities, including persons with disabilities and other marginalized groups, have a genuine and accessible voice in shaping and reviewing project delivery through a functioning feedback and complaints mechanism.

Key Responsibilities:

i) MEAL System Design and Management

  • Develop and implement the project’s full Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Plan, and keep it updated throughout the project cycle.
  • Design and maintain data-collection tools (registers, screening/camp forms, referral forms, complaint forms) that capture results disaggregated in line with the Log Frame.
  • Set up and administer the project’s Database Management, ensuring camp, screening, surgical, referral and training data are entered, cleaned and backed up in a timely manner.
  • Track progress against all Log Frame indicators and flag off-track indicators early.
  • Maintain and regularly update the project risk register, in coordination with the Project Manager.
  • Support Program Manager to prepare standard operation plan (SOP) of the activities.

ii) Reporting and Compliance

  • Prepare, or coordinate inputs for, all MEAL-related deliverables in the Reporting Plan, including: the Indicator Tracking Report and Activity Plan Report, the Quarterly and Annual
  • Project Reports, the updated M&E Plan and updated Project Risk Register, the Annual Reflection Report, and the monthly project update and plan.
  • Work closely with the Program Manager and Admin & Finance Officer to ensure narrative and financial reporting are consistent and submitted to CBM Global on schedule.
  • Maintain project records, data and documentation in line with the contract’s requirement, and ensure data is available for audit or monitoring visits on request.
  • Support preparation for internal and external audits, donor monitoring visits, including organizing evidence and facilitating access to community-level data.
  • Prepare and submit the datae as requested for funding organization.

iii) Accountability, Community Engagement and Feedback

  • Establish and manage an accessible community feedback and complaints mechanism (complaint boxes, providing contact details, telephone log, suggestion box) at base hospitals, eye/ear camps and community events.
  • Ensure feedback and complaints are logged, reviewed, responded to, and reported at least quarterly.
  • Facilitate regular consultations with beneficiaries, local Organizations of Persons with Disabilities and community leaders to assess service effectiveness, and ensure their input feeds into project adaptation.
  • Coordinate for community-level learning and sharing sessions, and document lessons learned for internal reflection.

iv) Safeguarding-Related MEAL Duties

  • Support the Disability Inclusion Officer in implementing and monitoring the project’s safeguarding reporting, investigation and response procedures, including tracking the required face-to-face safeguarding training for staff.
  • Ensure any safeguarding, fraud or other substantial risk incident identified through MEAL processes.
  • Ensure Data Protection standards to all personal data collected through MEAL processes (informed consent, secure storage, anonymization/pseudonymization before sharing), and report any personal data breach within 48 hours.

v) Evaluations and Learning

  • Coordinate logistics, data provision and stakeholder engagement for the project’s Baseline, Mid-Term and Final/End-Term Evaluations, working with the appointed independent evaluators/consultants.
  • Uphold the principles of quality, accuracy, utility, participation, ownership, ethics, reliability, transparency, cost-effectiveness, and impartiality.
  • Document and help produce project case studies, blogs, newsletter and accessible success stories (audio/video/print), in coordination with the Program Manager and Disability Inclusion Officer.

vi) Disability and Gender Inclusion in MEAL

  • Ensure all data collection, analysis and reporting is disaggregated as demand by the project and findings are used to identify and close equity gaps in service access.
  • Work with partners and stakeholders to ensure MEAL processes (data collection tools, feedback mechanisms, evaluation participation) are accessible and participatory for persons with disabilities.

vii) Coordination and Capacity Building

  • Provide MEAL-related orientation and on-the-job coaching to Community Eye Health Workers, base-hospital data collectors and volunteers on data quality, recording and reporting standards.
  • Represent the project’s MEAL function in Project Coordination Committee meetings, project review and reflection meetings.
  • Perform other MEAL and programme-quality-related duties requested by the Project Manager or NNJS management in support of project objectives.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in Public Health, Statistics, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • At least 3 years of professional experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) or M&E roles within an I/NGO, preferably in health, disability inclusion or community development programming.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and managing data-collection systems and databases, and contribute donor-standard quarterly/annual narrative and indicator reports.
  • Experience supporting or coordinating external evaluations, audits or reviews.
  • Prior experience working in Karnali Province or similar remote/hard-to-reach contexts is an advantage.
  • Experience working with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) or on disability-inclusive programming is strongly preferred.

Skills and Competencies

  • Sound understanding and skills in qualitative and data collection, management and analysis.
  • Strong data management and analysis skills, including proficiency with mobile/digital data-collection tools, data management and analysis software.
  • Sound understanding of log frames, theory of change, and indicator design, including disaggregation by sex, age and disability.
  • Working knowledge of safeguarding, data protection and accountability.
  • Facilitation, coaching and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work respectfully and effectively with community members, persons with disabilities, government officials, and partners.
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently within Karnali Province, including to remote hill and mountain districts.

Nabil Bank, established in 1984, is a market leader in Nepal’s banking sector. We are dedicated to be Nepal’s most trusted and future-ready Bank. Upholding our brand promise, “Together Ahead”, we invite highly talented, motivated, and qualified Nepali citizens to apply for the following position:

Position : Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
Level : Senior Manager (M4) and Above

Job Summary

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) is a Board-facing strategic executive responsible for providing independent oversight and leadership of the Bank’s enterprise-wide risk management and risk strategy. The CRO leads the Integrated Risk Management Framework (IRMF), ensuring effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of material risks in line with the Bank’s risk appetite, strategic objectives, and regulatory requirements.

As the Head of Risk Management and Member-Secretary of the Board-level Risk Management Committee (RMC), CRO provides independent risk advice to the Board and Senior Management and oversees key areas including capital and stress testing, digital and cyber risk, climate and emerging risks, model governance, and operational resilience, while promoting a strong risk culture and supporting sustainable business growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Risk Governance, Strategy & Board Advisory

  • Develop, lead and continuously enhance the Bank’s long- term Enterprise Risk Strategy, IRMF, and Risk Appetite Framework, aligned with the Board approved Risk Appetite, Risk Tolerance, and three lines of defense model.
  • Advise the Board and Senior Management on strategic and emerging risks, including risk implications of business plans and major business initiatives, and provide independent challenge where appropriate.
  • Establish and monitor risk limits, KRIs, dashboards, escalation and breach management frameworks, ensuring alignment with the Bank’s risk profile and regulatory requirements.
  • Review and enhance risk policies and control frameworks and provide periodic enterprise risk and emerging risk reports to the Board.

2. Credit Risk Leadership

  • Provide strategic oversight of credit risk, portfolio quality, sector and concentration risk, counterparty risk, sovereign exposure, and climate-related credit risk.
  • Oversee credit risk models, credit scorecards, early warning systems, watch list governance, NPA forecasting, recovery trend analysis and portfolio risk optimization.
  • Monitor the overall risk profile, asset quality, and portfolio concentration and strengthen risk analytics and emerging risk identification.

3. Market, Liquidity & Treasury Risk

  • Oversee Interest Rate Risk in Banking Book (IRRBB), foreign exchange, investment, Asset-Liability Management (ALM) and liquidity risks, transfer pricing risk including contingency funding and behavioral modelling.
  • Ensure effective macroeconomic scenario analysis and stress testing of market and liquidity exposures.
  • Provide oversight of compliance, AML/CFT, and information security risks as part of the Bank’s enterprise-wide risk framework.

4. Operational Resilience & Non-Financial Risk

  • Establish oversight frameworks for operational resilience, business continuity, disaster recovery, third-party/outsourcing, fraud, conduct, reputation, physical security, and crisis management risks.

5. Digital, Technology & Cyber Risk

  • Provide independent oversight of cyber, information security, cloud, digital banking, data governance / privacy, Artificial Intelligence, model, FinTech partnership, and technology investment risks.
  • Establish appropriate governance for technology and AI-enabled risk models.

6. Climate, ESG & Emerging Risks

  • Lead the development of the Bank’s climate and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) risk management framework, covering physical and transition risks, green financing, sustainability considerations, and climate stress testing.
  • Identify and assess emerging risks that may affect the Bank’s resilience and long-term sustainability.

7. Capital & Balance Sheet Management

  • Provide oversight of ICAAP, capital forecasting, capital and reverse stress testing, recovery planning, economic capital, Risk Adjusted Return on Capital (RAROC), and risk-based pricing to ensure adequate capital and risk-adjusted returns.
  • Ensure alignment of capital with the Bank’s overall risk profile.

8. Model Risk Management

  • Establish and oversee the Bank’s Model Risk Management Framework covering model governance, validation, performance monitoring, and periodic review.
  • Oversee IFRS 9/ECL, credit, scorecard, stress-testing, and AI models, ensuring robust methodologies, assumptions, and outputs.
  • Ensure independent validation, backtesting, sensitivity analysis, and timely remediation of model-related findings, with appropriate integration into risk reporting, provisioning, capital planning, and ICAAP.

9. Enterprise – wide Risk Reporting

  • Ensure timely and comprehensive risk reporting to the Board and Senior Management through risk dashboards, heat maps, emerging risk reports, scenario analysis, top 20 Enterprise Risks and forward-looking enterprise risk outlooks to support strategic and business decisions.

10. Regulatory & Supervisory Engagement

  • Lead regulatory and supervisory engagement, ensuring compliance with applicable NRB directives and laws, effective coordination with regulators and auditors, and timely and accurate regulatory risk reporting, including Basel and resolution planning requirements.
  • Represent the Bank in relevant regulatory and industry forums and ensure effective management of supervisory reviews and inspections.

11. Risk Culture & Awareness

  • Promote a strong enterprise-wide risk culture through risk culture assessments, training, certification, conduct risk programmes, appropriate incentive alignment, speak-up mechanisms, and risk awareness initiatives.
  • Drive risk awareness, accountability, and appropriate risk-taking behaviour across the Bank and support organizational transformation and cross-functional collaboration.

12. Cross-functional Governance

  • Provide leadership and/or participate in relevant risk governance forums, including Executive Risk, Operational Risk, Market Risk, Model Risk, New Product Approval, Information Security, ALCO, Credit, Credit Control, Compliance, AML/CFT, and IT Steering Committees, as applicable.
  • Ensure strong coordination between business, support, and control functions and build appropriate capabilities, systems, and talent within the risk function.
  • Evaluate credit proposals, new products, strategic initiatives, and major business decisions from an independent risk perspective and ensure appropriate risk mitigation measures are in place.

13. Performance Management

  • Establish measurable risk management outcomes, including maintaining risk within Board-approved appetite, strengthening early warning and stress-testing capabilities, reducing material operational losses, ensuring timely closure of audit and regulatory observations, and maintaining compliance with regulatory requirements.

14. Risk Management Committee -Member-Secretary

  • Act as Member-Secretary of the Board-level Risk Management Committee (RMC).
  • Coordinate RMC meetings, including agenda preparation, circulation of relevant risk reports and materials, and effective communication with Committee members.
  • Ensure effective Board-level risk reporting and communication and monitor and track implementation of decisions and directives of the RMC.

Qualification & Experience

  • Master’s Degree in Finance, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Risk Management, Banking, Business Administration, or related discipline from a recognized University/Institution.
  • Minimum 15 years of banking experience, with at least 8 years in progressively senior risk management/leadership roles.
  • Currently serving in a senior risk leadership role in Risk Review, Monitoring and Management, such as Head of Credit Risk, Chief Risk Officer (CRO), or Deputy CRO.
  • Candidates with Professional certifications such as Financial / Professional Risk Manager (FRM/ PRM), CFA, CA & Cybersecurity Risk will be given preference.
  • Demonstrated experience interacting with Boards, regulators, auditors, and rating agencies.
  • Proven experience in enterprise risk management, Basel implementation, ICAAP, IFRS 9/ECL, stress testing, model governance, and digital risk.
  • Experience leading large cross-functional teams and driving enterprise-wide risk transformation.

The Position:

Under the overall supervision of the International Operations Manager, guidance and direct supervision of the Finance Associate, the Finance Assistant is responsible for implementing the organizational financial rules and regulations in the UNFPA Country Office (CO). S/he delivers quality financial services to the CO staff, ensuring effective and transparent financial management. How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The Finance Assistant will provide overall financial management support to the Finance Associate in the Operations Team. The Finance Assistant works in close collaboration with the operations, programme and project teams in the UNFPA CO; s/he facilitates smooth operations, helps resolve any complex financial issues, and ensures high quality and accuracy of work.

You would be responsible for:

1. Implementation of operational strategies:

3. Acting as FACE focal point for all the FACE forms of all IPs:

The Program Officer for the Active Citizenship Department plays a central role in driving YUWA’s mandate on youth political participation, with primary responsibility for the Political Participation of Persons with Disabilities (Y-PWD) project. The role requires strong program design, implementation, cohort management, research coordination, and cross-organizational collaboration. The Program Officer will also contribute to YUWA’s core political participation programs and provide support to other departmental initiatives when needed.

2. Purpose of the Position

The Program Officer is responsible for designing, implementing, and managing the Y-PWD Project and supporting the wider Active Citizenship portfolio. This includes fostering meaningful youth civic engagement, facilitating disability-inclusive political participation, coordinating with cohort members and consortium partners, and developing thematic resources and tools. The role ensures donor compliance, timely reporting, field-level monitoring, and collaborative execution of programmatic activities.

3. Key Responsibilities

A. Program Design, Planning, and Implementation (Primary – Y-PWD Project)

  • Lead day-to-day program design and implementation of the Y-PWD Project with minimal guidance, ensuring alignment with departmental and organizational strategies.
  • Co-design Detailed Implementation Plans (DIPs), activity plans, and engagement frameworks in collaboration with the Department Coordinator and Executive Board.
  • Coordinate cohort-based activities, including inception sessions, political participation trainings, exposure visits, and continuous engagement planning.
  • Support, when required, activities under Y-ERISID and department-led core programs.

B. Cohort and Team Supervision

  • Directly supervise the Cohort Coordinator assigned to the Y-PWD Project, ensuring clear task delegation, quality delivery, and accountability.
  • Act as the focal point for cohort management, including recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement planning for persons with disabilities and the other cohort members.

C. Coordination, Representation, and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Represent YUWA in consortium meetings for the Y-PWD project and act as the primary technical focal person.
  • Engage with government representatives, youth networks, CSOs, disability groups, and other stakeholders to advance political participation objectives.

D. Reporting, Monitoring, Documentation, and Compliance

  • Take the lead in preparing donor-required reports, quarterly updates, and documentation for the Y-PWD Project.
  • Conduct regular field monitoring visits and produce high-quality field reports, documentation notes, and reflective summaries.

E. Finance, Logistics, and Administration

  • Take responsibility for budget tracking, expenditure monitoring, and adherence to financial guidelines for the Y-PWD Project.
  • Coordinate with the Finance Officer for procurement, payments, documentation, logistical arrangements, and compliance processes.

4. Reporting & Line Management

Direct Supervisor: Project Focal (Executive Board)

Secondary Oversight: Executive Board (for strategic guidance and project approvals)

Supervises: Cohort Coordinator, interns/volunteers as designated

Collaborates with: Program Assistant, Communications Team, Finance Team, and other departmental program team as required.

5. Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, Political Science, Development Studies, Gender Studies, or a related field with a strong understanding of Nepal’s political context, youth civic issues, disability rights,
  • 1–2 years of experience in civic engagement, youth mobilization, disability inclusion, or political participation programming (highly preferred).
  • Experience working with or engaging persons with disabilities is an advantage.
  • Experience in program design, field coordination, cohort engagement, or consortium-based work preferred.

6. Required Competencies

  • Strong understanding of disability-inclusive development and political participation.
  • Ability to design and implement programs with minimal supervision.
  • Strong coordination, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Understanding of budgeting, procurement coordination, and financial compliance.
  • Commitment to safeguarding, ethical conduct, respect, and inclusion

The Program Officer must adhere to YUWA’s safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, and anti-harassment policies. Ensuring the safety and meaningful participation of young people, including persons with disabilities, is a non-negotiable aspect of the role.

Job Title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Associate
Department: Program/MEAL

Project Area: Taplejung, Solukhumbu and Khotang
Type of Job: Full-time with frequent field visits
Reports to: MEAL Manager/ District Project Manager

Action for Nepal

AFN is a high performing, community-centric organization building healthy, educated communities in Nepal through effective projects, sound strategies, efficient processes and successful partnerships. AFN is committed to respecting, protecting and promoting internationally recognized human rights including civil and political, economic, social and cultural rights, with particular emphasis on gender equality, the protection of children, people with a disability and the rights of minorities and vulnerable and marginalized groups.

Position overview:

AF Nepal is seeking two qualified and experienced MEAL Associates to support and strengthen project-specific MEAL systems. The MEAL Associates will contribute to results-based monitoring, data collection and management, data quality assurance, analysis, reporting, accountability, learning, and evidence generation across AF Nepal’s projects. They will work closely with project teams to ensure quality data and evidence are systematically generated, documented, and used to inform decision-making, program improvement, accountability, and organizational learning.

Duties and Responsibilities:

A. Monitoring System Implementation

  • Support the Project Officer in implementing field-level activities in line with the project design and M&E framework, ensuring alignment with the theory of change and intended outcomes.
  • Assist in tracking indicators across all outputs and monitoring progress of activities against approved plans.
  • Maintain and regularly update indicator tracking sheets and project databases.
  • Coordinate with district authorities, rural municipalities, health facilities, and other stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate data collection for all project activities.
  • Contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, quarterly activity plans, and detailed activity schedules in coordination with the project team.
  • Plan, implement, and coordinate project activities to ensure quality standards across AFN programs.
  • Participate in joint supervision visits and in MSS assessments.
  • Support data collection and documentation for MSS assessments, facility improvement plans, and supportive supervision.
  • Document MSS findings and track follow-up actions.
  • Ensure activities are implemented effectively and on time in accordance with approved project documents.
  • Assist in the preparation and timely submission of activity reports, quarterly progress reports, and required data as per reporting timelines.
  • Ensure adherence to AFN policies and procedures across all field-level activities.
  • Maintain regular communication with the project team and provide field-level support to program implementation.
  • Coordinate with local stakeholders and contribute to planning for project sustainability.
  • Support to organize and schedule meetings/events, and maintain agendas and minutes.
  • Support program growth and development initiatives.

B. Data Collection, Management, and Documentation

  • Collect and verify data from Municipalities, Health facilities, FCHVs and Community activities
  • Ensure quality data in terms of Accuracy, Completeness, Timeliness
  • Support disability-disaggregated data recording and reporting.
  • Support training and follow-up on HMIS/PAMS reporting and data review and management practices.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities, collect data, prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reports and ensure adherence to project plans.
  • Compile field monitoring findings and Data summaries and visualization.
  • Provide regular and timely updates of the field activities and document the information;
  • Document stories of change, best practices and learning from the project.
  • Ensure quality assurance of the project activities in the district in terms of logistic management, content, delivery of the activities and documentation.
  • Proper documentation of all the relevant references and materials.

C. Safeguarding, Risk management and Inclusion

  • Ensure all project activities comply with the organization’s safeguarding and inclusion policies, including Child Safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH), and Gender
  • Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) standards.
  • Contribute to assessing, mitigating and reporting on all risks, including risks of child abuse and exploitation and sexual abuse and exploitation, in the project area.
  • Support the implementation of effective incident reporting mechanisms both within the health centers and in the community.
  • Ensure immediate reporting to AFN of any incident of abuse and exploitation.
  • Follow directives of AFN for follow up required regarding incidents, including reporting to concerned authorities;
  • Ensure safety of survivor, confidentiality and survivor centered approach.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Statistics, or related field
  • Minimum 1-2 years of post-qualification experience Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL/M&E).
  • Familiarity with government of Nepal’s HMIS/PAMS systems, Data collection tools and project reporting formats.
  • Experience working with Local governments and Health systems in Nepal.

Required Skills

  • Strong data analysis and skills on statistical tools (KOBO, SPSS, R etc)
  • Excellent computer skills, including Microsoft Office package
  • Ability to work in field settings
  • Good communication skills
  • Analytical and problem-solving ability
  • Report writing and documentation
  • Fluency in Nepali and English

The MEAL Associate may be assigned other reasonable duties and responsibilities by the supervisor or senior management in accordance with AF Nepal’s organizational priorities and program needs.

Inclusive Policy: AF Nepal encourages applications from women, people with disabilities, ethnic minorities, and marginalized communities.

Action for Nepal is an equal opportunity employer. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the advertisement might be closed prior to the deadline, if suitable candidates apply.
